Permits shall not be required for the following: Building: 1. One-story detached accessory structures used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses and similar uses, provided that the floor area does not exceed than 120 square feet. ... 2. Fences not over 7 feet high unless used as a pool, spa, or hot tub barrier. ... 3. Oil derricks. 4. Retaining walls that are not over 4 feet in height measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless supporting a surcharge or impounding Class I, II, or II-A liquids. 5. Water tanks supported directly on grade if the capacity does not exceed 5,000 gallons and the ratio of height to diameter or width does not exceed 2:1. 6. Sidewalks and driveways not more than 30 inches above adjacent grade, and not over any basement or story below and are not part of an accessible route. 7. Painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work. 8. Temporary motion picture, television and theater stage sets and scenery. 9. Prefabricated swimming pools accessory to a Group R-3 occupancy that are less than 24 inches deep, do not exceed 5,000 gallons and are installed entirely above ground. ... 10. Shade cloth structures constructed for nursery or agricultural purposes, not including service systems. 11. Swings and other playground equipment accessory to detached one- and two-family dwellings. 12. Window awnings supported by an exterior wall that do not project more than 54 inches from the exterior wall and do not require additional support of Group R-3 and U occupancies. 13. Non-fixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height.

page.meta: Commercial bathroom partitions delivered to Stockton job sites. Price your restroom in five questions and see the California and city rules that apply.
page.lead: Commercial bathroom partitions for Stockton warehouses, food processing plants, schools and medical offices, shipped by freight to your job site.
page.stall_bullet: - **How many stalls:** Stockton uses California's rules, which set the number of toilets and urinals by how many people use the building. The table below shows what that means.
page.permit_bullet: - **Permits:** Stockton requires a building permit to alter or remodel a building. Its list of work that needs none covers "painting, papering, tiling, carpeting, cabinets, counter tops and similar finish work" and "non-fixed and movable fixtures, cases, racks, counters and partitions not over 5 feet 9 inches in height". It doesn't name toilet partitions, so ask the Building & Life Safety Division (209-937-8561) whether your replacement needs one. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.confirm_office: the City of Stockton Building & Life Safety Division
page.stalls_intro: Stockton counts toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. It isn't the number of staff or of visitors in a day. Half are counted as men and half as women, and California's rules require urinals in the men's room. Every toilet needs a stall, and urinals need screens between them. The women's room must have at least as many toilets as the men's room has toilets and urinals together.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for new buildings, additions and changes of use that bring in more people. An office or shop with 50 people or fewer may have a single one-person restroom. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, California's plumbing rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, and a restaurant dining room or a classroom at one per 30 square feet. Your architect or the City of Stockton Building & Life Safety Division sets the final number.
page.install_rule: In Stockton, contractors need a city business license and pay the city's business tax. California requires its contractor license, usually the C-61/D-34 class, for partition installs of $1,000 or more, and at any price when the job needs workers or a permit. You don't need a permit to buy partitions.
page.faq_install_extra: In Stockton the contractor needs a California contractor license for jobs of $1,000 or more.
page.public_jobs_bullet: - **Public jobs:** California requires the state-set wage on public jobs over $1,000, including city and school district work. For a carpenter in San Joaquin County that is $68.58 an hour plus $34.95 in benefits.
page.sales_tax_bullet: - **Sales tax:** 9% in Stockton: 7.25% statewide, 0.5% for the county transportation authority and 1.25% in three city taxes.
page.buyers_extra: - **Colleges and public buildings:** phenolic or stainless steel that stands up to heavy daily use.
